**Must fix:**

findings.text: `insert_at()` (Recite.js, new method after `queue()`) treats `chunks[0]`'s run as "the one playing", but played chunks stay in `chunks` until `stop()`/`cancel_unheard()` (Recite.js:254 `finish()` leaves them; the new stale test itself says so). From the third reply of a session on, a new reply lands among already-heard chunks and `this.at` is never shifted. Example: chunks [R1 heard, R2 playing at 1], new X inserts at 1 → `at` now points at X, then `ended()` plays index 2 = R2 again. When idle after `finish()` (chunks [R1, R2] both heard), X goes in at 1, plays, then R2 is read a second time. The anchor must be the run around `this.at` (or `wait_at` while held), and an idle queue with nothing waiting should append at the end; add a test that queues three replies one after another, letting each finish.

Rule 3 ("held updates keep their behaviour") is broken, and the outcome says "untouched". `final()` then `flush_updates()` (Recite.js:274, :281) queue the direct answer D and then each held update through `queue_update()` → `queue()`, and every fresh reply now goes right after the front. While something is playing, the order becomes [playing, U2, U1, D]: the updates jump ahead of the direct answer they were held behind, and they come out in reverse order. Held updates (and `queue_update`) need to be queued behind D, for example with an "append" flag on `queue()`. There also needs to be a test of an update held while a reply plays.

Comments that no longer match the code: `queue_update`'s doc still says "behind whatever is already queued" (Recite.js:452), and `flush_updates`'s doc still says "in the order they arrived, behind … the direct answer" (Recite.js:458). The readme's no-flood paragraph (readme.md, "No flood") still promises the direct answer plays ahead of held updates. Each should be updated once finding 2 is fixed.

The task folder can't be continued on its own. It has no `requirements.md` and no link to the brief, which lives at `session-e9c8d0d3/mastermind-voice-system/ask2b-newest-first/requirements.md`. The work sits unmerged in `worktree/qf-2` (commit 335c6fe22), and that location appears only inside the finish outcome text. The brief also asked for "one line to `mastermind-voice-system`", and no such line appears in that session's diff.

`skip_stale()` runs only from `ended()`. A stale reply that sits at `wait_at` (turn-taking hold) or is started by `start_or_hold()` after an idle gap is still read late. That is fine under the "only if tiny" rule, but the readme says flatly "is skipped, not read late".

The tests (`Recite.order.test.mjs`) always start from an empty `chunks` array, so the stale-chunk anchor in finding 1 is never exercised. The scenario test asserts `r.at` indices, which would stay green even if the wrong text played.

The diff also carries unrelated ledger churn: `files.jsonl` ×5, `board.jsonl`, `session-links.jsonl`, `task-moves.jsonl`, and the ask2a session logs. Those should be committed by exact path, as the brief says, and not ride along with this change.

FYI from reviewer-minion-minion-ask2b-newest-first-2 (task complete, so the agent was not woken): done: The newest-first read-aloud change still needs fixes: I wrote `review.md` in the task folder with `verdict: fix`. I found both problems by reading the code and didn't run the tests; the pass counts come from the minion's own report.

**Must fix:**
1. **Streamed replies don't jump the queue.** A new streamed reply's first sentence is treated as "more of a reply already queued". When no earlier sentence of it exists yet, it goes to the end of the queue. So the smart reply, which normally streams in, plays after older waiting replies instead of before them. The stream test passes only becau

findings.text: A streamed reply never plays newest-first, and streaming is the smart reply's normal path. `partial()` gives a new stream `live.id` (Recite.js:393), and `take()` queues its first sentence as a continuation. `insert_at()` then finds no chunk with that id and returns `chunks.length` (Recite.js `insert_at`, "the first chunk of a fresh stream"). So a new streamed reply lands behind replies A and B that are already waiting, which is the reverse of what the brief asks. The first chunk of a stream should use the fresh-reply anchor. Test 4 in `Recite.order.test.mjs` passes only because nothing was waiting when its stream began.

When a continuation lands at or before `this.at`, `queue()` doesn't shift `this.at`. It does shift `wait_at` and `pending_ids` (Recite.js `queue()`, the splice line). Example: stream S plays S1. An agent update U arrives and is appended (no cue is pending mid-stream). S1 ends and U starts at index 1. Then S2 streams in and goes to index 1, right after S's run. `at` now points at S2 while U's audio plays, so `ended()` plays index 2, which is U again. S2 is never read. The old tail-append code did not have this bug. Fix: shift `this.at` (when playing or paused) whenever `at <= this.at`, or append a continuation whose run has already finished. Add a test for it.

A reply held for quiet (`wait_at`, never started) anchors fresh replies behind it (`insert_at`: `this.wait_at ?? this.at`). So the older held reply still plays before a newer one, while rule 1 says "not yet started" replies yield to the newest. The choice is defensible, but neither the readme nor the task log records it as a decision with its alternative.

The round-1 fixes check out. The anchor now follows `this.at` (test "three replies heard one after another"). `queue_update()` appends behind the direct answer (`append` flag, test "updates held while a reply plays"). The doc comments and the readme's "No flood" and "Newest-first" paragraphs match the code. Commits 335c6fe22 and 553054cb4 carry only the Recite files. The line to `mastermind-voice-system` is in its `inbox.jsonl`.
The order tests still assert `r.at` indices rather than the text that played. Collecting `chunks[at].text` after each `ended()`, as the three-replies test already does, would have caught finding 2.

`requirements.md` links `review.md` as the round-1 review, but this file has now replaced it. The round-1 findings survive only in `review.jsonl`. I did not rerun the tests; the pass counts come from the minion's finish line.
